title: Network radio shows: Old Gold with Allan Jones and Wildroot Cream Oil
summary: In 1944-45 the band had a short Old Gold show with Allan Jones and then its own weekly Wildroot show that travelled with the band.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: Good, good. Woody, what about the principal radio shows you had in earlier days? You had a couple of them, didn't you, cigarettes and Wildroot Cream Oil and --

Yeah. Well, the first one, actually, was -- the first one that we had a series, a matter of weeks, was Old Gold cigarettes, and it was an incongruous mating, I think. It was our band along with a former movie singer and actor, the guy that did -- was famous for Donkey Serenade, Allen Jones.

Yes. So, he was a kind of legit singer, and with a jazz band it really was kind of a strange mating. As a matter of fact, the original premise of the show was, I think, his vocals and the band of Frankie Carl, the pianist. And for some reason or other, maybe it was because some record of ours was selling, -- I'll never know the reason, actually, but we wound up on the show and it turned out pretty well. And it wasn't too much later, in the following season, we finally got our complete own show and that was for the Wildroot Cream Oil hair dressing. And we did about 13 weeks, I think. And then, when we concluded our stint, Nat Cole took
took over the show with the trio.
Now, both of these were network shows.
What year was that first one?
'44, I believe, and the next one was '45.
Uh-huh. That's how Wildroot came around.
Wildroot travelled with us, which made it very -- it was a great thing for the band. Once a week, and it emanated from wherever we were.
